cards.text: Absalom's rebellion is over, and all through the tribes of Israel, people are arguing. The king rescued them from their enemies and delivered them from the Philistines, they say. But now he's fled the land because of Absalom.

cards.question: Absalom, the man Israel anointed over them, has died in battle. So what are the people of Israel asking each other?

answers.text: Why no one talks of restoring the king
Who they should anoint as king next
Whether to go fight the Philistines

cards.text: And all that talk from Israel reaches David where he's staying. It's the whole office group chat talking about the boss, and NOBODY remembered the boss is IN the chat.

cards.question: David sends Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, to ask the elders of ___ why they should be the last to restore the king to his palace.
What does David tell the priests to remind the elders of Judah about?

answers.text: They are his own flesh and blood
They swore to serve him forever
Their land belongs to the king

cards.text: Then David adds a message for Amasa, the man Absalom put over his army in place of Joab (2 Samuel 17:25). Joab is the commander of David's own army (2 Samuel 8:16).

cards.question: David swears that from now on, Amasa will be the ___ of his army.

cards.text: In place of JOAB. Friend, I know a little something about getting swapped out for a shiny new model, so I'm not laughing at anybody here.

cards.question: David's message splits the men of Judah, with half for him and half against him.
So what message do the men of Judah send back to the king?

cards.text: So the king heads back. When he reaches the Jordan, the men of Judah come to Gilgal to meet him.

cards.question: The men of Judah come to Gilgal to stop David from crossing the Jordan.

cards.text: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurries down with the men of Judah to meet King David. Friend, this is the man who cursed David and threw stones at him when David fled Jerusalem (2 Samuel 16:5-13).

cards.question: Shimei comes down to meet the king with a thousand men of Benjamin.
Someone else rushes down to the Jordan with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. Who is it?

answers.text: Ziba the steward of Saul's house

cards.text: They cross at the ford to carry over the king's household and do what is good in his sight. Then Shimei crosses the Jordan and reaches the king.

cards.question: When Shimei reaches King David, what does he do?

answers.text: He falls down before the king
He stands back and keeps quiet

cards.question: Shimei is down before David. What does he ask the king?

answers.text: To give him a place at court
To give him back his land

cards.question: Shimei insists he did nothing wrong on the day David left Jerusalem.

cards.text: He owns it: "For your servant knows that I have sinned." Last time Shimei saw David he was throwing rocks, and now he's throwing HIMSELF on the ground.
And he says here he is today, the first of all the house of Joseph to come down and meet the king.
But Abishai son of Zeruiah, one of David's commanders, has something to say about that (2 Samuel 18:2).

cards.question: Abishai son of Zeruiah tells David to show Shimei mercy.

cards.text: Abishai asks, "Shouldn't Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD's anointed?"
David answers, "Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today?" ADVERSARIES, friend, that's a word you save for the other army!

cards.question: David asks whether any man should be put to death in Israel today. What does David say he knows about today?

answers.text: Today he is king over Israel
Today is a holy feast day

cards.question: So the king gives Shimei his answer: you shall not ___.
To back up his word, the king swears an oath to Shimei.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Trust me, friend, there's more coming out of this oven.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "For your servant knows that I have sinned.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The group-chat joke ('NOBODY remembered the boss is IN the chat') turns the talk into gossip the people didn't mean David to hear. In 2 Samuel 19:9-11 the talk is about restoring the king, and the text never says it wasn't meant to reach him. The comparison adds a slip-up that isn't in the passage, and it could leave the baker thinking the talk was against David.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 6 says Absalom put Amasa over his army in place of Joab, and that Joab is the commander of David's army. Card 7 then asks what Amasa will be 'of his army', and the setup has already used the word 'commander'. That rules out 'treasurer' and 'scribe' before the baker picks. The card should give the context (Amasa led Absalom's army) without naming the role David is about to give him.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 8 only goes back over 2 Samuel 19:13, which cards 6 and 7 already covered. It adds no new part of the passage. It's a reaction card that doesn't move the baker forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next moment.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'So I'm not laughing at anybody here' explains the joke right after it lands. It also reads like a nice dad being pleasant instead of a real laugh.

The joke calls back to Papa Dorin being swapped out for a shiny new stamper. The docs only confirm that bakers know about the junk drawer from onboarding. They don't say whether onboarding covers him being replaced by the new stamper.
findings.question: Does onboarding tell bakers that Papa Dorin was replaced by a new stamper, so a callback to being 'swapped out for a shiny new model' works without a setup earlier in the lesson?

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Ziba the steward of Saul's house', is twice as long as the wrong answers ('Hushai the Archite', 'Ittai the Gittite'). It's also the only one with a role that fits a man arriving with fifteen sons and twenty servants, so it stands out. Either all three answers should carry a title or role of similar length, or none should.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Card 8 mostly goes back over what cards 5 and 7 already answered: Shimei falls down before the king, and he admits he did wrong. The only new piece is the quote from 2 Samuel 19:20. As written, the card works as a recap. The quote and the joke should carry the passage forward, for example by joining with card 9's 'first of all the house of Joseph' moment.
The closing line copies the doc's example almost word for word ('And that's where we'll ... for now. Trust me, friend, ...'). It isn't a fresh line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
